messages:
Sahil: Quick share — AWQ bakeoff on the new model variant turned up a pretty localized regression. Aggregate eval PPL up ~4.6% vs float baseline, but digging in shows two attention heads with heavy outlier channels (layer 23 head 6, layer 27 head 2). Anyone else seeing similar headwise spikes? https://evals.internal/runs/rl-2317 :thinking:

Maria: Ack saw that briefly, didn't grok the head-level yet. Do you have per-channel activation histograms? :mag:

Sahil: Yes — here's a small excerpt from the analyzer output (trimmed):

```
# activation_hist summary (keys dot queries)
layer 23 head 6: tail_mass=0.023 max=12.8 mean=0.14 outlier_score=4.8
layer 27 head 2: tail_mass=0.029 max=15.3 mean=0.11 outlier_score=5.1
other heads: tail_mass <= 0.004
```

When I force those channels to float16 in the AWQ pipeline (weights quantized except those channel ranges) the PPL recovers ~70% of the delta and long-form hallucination rate drops noticeably.

Alex: Nice find. Instead of full skip, can we apply a per-head rescale+clamp during quant (headwise multiplier) so we keep int8 everywhere but adjust scaling for the offending channels?

Jen: From an ops viewpoint we need the perf delta for Dedicated profiles. Even small FP16 exceptions can increase kernel counts and memory pressure.

Samir: Ran a micro-canary on a Dedicated pool (same GPU type as staging). Metrics: p95 latency +3.2% at 2048 context, median +0.9%. Cost delta ~+1.8% token-equivalent because of extra memory copies. Throughput unaffected for small batch sizes.

Sahil: Thanks Samir. Proposed mitigation order: 1) per-channel clamp/rescale in AWQ quantizer (cheap, keeps int8), 2) temporary per-head FP16 gate for the minimal set (if 1 fails), 3) layer-skip fallback if >N outlier channels in a layer. Also add detection to quant-scan to emit per-head outlier scores for automatic skiplist generation.

Maria: Sounds good. If we go with per-head clamp, we should capture a reproducible subset of prompts that trigger the spike and add to our eval set to avoid regressions later. I'll start building a probe set.

Sahil: Example skiplist config I tested (json format we can wire into runtime):

```
{
  "model": "redwood-mix-17b-awq-v1",
  "skiplist": [
    {"layer": 23, "head": 6, "strategy": "fp16_gate"},
    {"layer": 27, "head": 2, "strategy": "fp16_gate"}
  ],
  "autothreshold": {"outlier_score": 3.0}
}
```

Alex: Small UX note — surface these per-head flags in the model profile page (Console) with a short rationale so customers see why a mixed-precision exception exists.

QuantBot: Automated quant scan finished: register RL-2317. Detected outlier_score(s) >= 3.0 for the listed heads. Suggested action: per-channel clamp -> re-run AWQ.

Jen: Canary plan: create a staging-dedicated rollout with the skiplist enabled on 5% capacity for 24h. Gate: end-to-end eval delta < 1.0% on our hallucination/QA suite and p95 latency increase < 5%. If pass, increase to 50% and then full.

Samir: I'll open a runtime PR to support per-head FP16 gating and a lightweight per-head clamp option in the quantizer. ETA: PR by EOD, tests tomorrow.

Sahil: Maria — can you run the full eval harness on the clamp variant when Samir posts PR? Capture both accuracy and hallucination heuristics + token-cost. Jen — can you schedule the canary once infra-bot gives green?

InfraBot: Canary cluster provisioning started for staging-dedicated-3. ETA 45m.

Sahil: Great — assign RL-2317 owners: Samir (runtime/PR), Maria (eval harness), Jen (canary/rollout). I'll update the ticket with the perf numbers and attach the failing prompt set. :thumbsup:
